### workspace kill --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace kill [--name WS] [--force] [--delete-remote] [--json] [project]

Kill a worktree project's session and remove its git worktree.
The inverse of 'workspace start'.

If no project is given (positionally or with --name), kills the workspace
the current directory is in: a worktree's .workspace-project marker, else the
active workspace whose root holds it. Outside any workspace it refuses
(not_in_workspace).

Refuses to remove a worktree with uncommitted changes to tracked files
or commits that haven't been pushed anywhere (untracked files don't
count). --force skips this check along with the confirmation prompt.

Deletes the local branch too when 'workspace start' created it (git branch -d,
which keeps a branch not merged into its upstream, or into HEAD without one).
A branch that existed before start is kept. With --force the branch is deleted
even if unmerged (git branch -D). --delete-remote also deletes the branch on its
upstream remote once it is merged into the default branch and holds no commits
the local branch lacks (any state with --force).

Options:
        --name NAME                  The worktree workspace to kill (default: the one detected from the current directory)
    -f, --force                      Skip confirmation, skip the uncommitted/unpushed-work check and the open
                                     pull request check, and delete an unmerged start-created branch (-D)
        --delete-remote              Also delete the branch on its upstream remote when start created it (any branch
                                     with --force), never an upstream of another name or the default branch; refuses
                                     over an open pull request (open_pull_request) unless --force
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of text, which goes
                                     to stderr; a refusal is the error envelope with a retry hint

Examples:
  workspace kill    # after a confirmation, end the worktree workspace you are in: its session and git worktree, and the branch start made if it is merged
  workspace kill myproject.worktree-PROJ-123    # the same for a named worktree workspace, from anywhere
  workspace kill --name myproject.worktree-PROJ-123 --json    # the same, naming it with a flag; one action document (it still asks first)
  workspace kill -f myproject.worktree-PROJ-123    # skip confirmation and the unsaved-work check, and force-delete the branch start made
  workspace kill -f --json myproject.worktree-PROJ-123    # scripted: no prompt, and the unsaved-work check is skipped too
  workspace kill --delete-remote    # also delete the branch on its remote
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace kill --bogus
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
invalid option: --bogus
--- end
### workspace kill --bogus --json
--- exit 1
--- stdout
{"schema_version":1,"ok":false,"error":"invalid option: --bogus","code":"usage"}
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace kill
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Error: No workspace found for $CWD. Run from inside a workspace or pass --name.
--- end
